notes.title: v1.2 : Local leaderboards, tweaked challenge scores, bugfixes
notes.content:
Hey, all you awesome beach cleaners!

We've just pushed the 1.2 update to everyone, which among other things adds this requested feature: Local Leaderboards.

You now have the choice to not post scores to the public leaderboards, and instead just track your scores locally. This option is at the bottom of the "New Game" screen, and defaults to the current behaviour (public).

Even if you do post your scores publicly, this feature means you can see your best 10 local scores as well, with the date/time you achieved them, so you can see the spread. Was that high score a one-off, or did you get really close to it last week? Maybe next time you'll beat it? :)

Just cycle through the Filter on the high score page, which now has 3 options "Global", "Friends", and "Local".

The full changes list is below, we hope you enjoy the update, and thanks for playing!

Full Change List:
[list]
[*] Option to not post scores to public leaderboards
[*] Best 10 local scores with timestamps (via high score filter option)
[*] Fixed high score previews not being visible on New Game screen in 4K
[*] Try to always provide a "Challenge" score when playing publicly; if you have no friends with better scores, display the next score above from Global leaderboards
[*]Fixed a potential bug with interleaved scores from different filters if you flipped through the high score options too quickly
[*] First-time tutorial experience tweaks
[/list]

notes.title: v1.1 update : save games and more!
notes.content:
We just released a fairly significant update which will be of particular interest to those of you playing long games!

[h1]Save & Resume[/h1]

Now when you bring up the in-game menu, there's a new option "Save and Exit", which does what you would expect! 

Now you can come back to your game later; when you next choose Start Game from the main menu you can just resume where you left off. The only limitation is you can't save in the middle of a storm, or when you have a block currently picked up; resuming in the middle of those is jarring. Finish the storm or place the block, then you can save.

[h1]More music variety[/h1]

We've mixed up the music selection a little to give more variety in each game mode; there are now [b]double [/b]the number of tracks available in each mode. 

Previously each game mode had its own dedicated track list, but since many people mostly play a single game mode, some nice tracks weren't getting into rotation. 

There is now some overlap between modes so you get more variety, although some tracks are still reserved for certain modes; e.g. the chill-out tracks of Free Play don't really work for the frantic pace of Time Attack.

[h1]Other minor issues[/h1]

[list]
[*] Improved error reporting & recovery of Steam connection problems
[*] Fixed a rare case of the first block visual being slightly out of alignment after game restart
[*] Fixed queued sound effects at the end of a game playing at the start of the next one
[/list]

We hope you enjoy the update!

notes.title: Hotfix 1.0.4.2 for in-game Steam overlay
notes.content:
We've just posted an important hotfix which fixes a bug that would cause you to lose your score if you opened the Steam overlay in the middle of a game. Our lame excuse is that we stupidly forgot to re-test the auto-pause on overlay feature after making some changes to the in-game menu, and none of the beta testers came across it either.

Sincere apologies to anyone affected by this! It's fixed now.

notes.title: Free Play Mode, wider beta
notes.content:
Hi everyone! 

The beta process has gone really well so far and we've made a ton of refinements to the game over the last few weeks. Big thanks to all our beta testers! We're opening the beta to more people next week as we head into the final straight before release. 

There are too many individual changes to mention since the beta started, but the headlines include:

 [list]
    [*]New no-pressure Free Play game mode (to go with Classic Mode and Time Attack)
    [*]Completely reworked and extended tutorials
    [*]Control system refinements to make everything feel better
    [*]Enhanced pollution effects and mechanics
[/list] 

All in all we're really happy with the way things are going. The new set of beta testers next week will help us test the new user experience again after all these changes. 

As for release, our target is still "Summer", which is intentionally vague :) We [i]could[/i] release the game right now - we don't have any more major changes left to make, but we do have a bit more polishing we want to do first. It's our first game, and even though it's small and fairly simple, we want it to be as good as we can make it. We'll most likely fix a hard date in the next month, and then focus on talking to anyone who will listen about it ahead of that date!

Thanks again to our testers and everyone who has shown an interest in Washed Up!
